title: Did Taylor Swift fans cause an earthquake?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: someone or something has a positive effect on you, making your life enjoyable

keywords.term: not be in the same league
keywords.def: (idiom) not nearly as good or important as someone or something else
similar (in size, amount or quality) to something else

sentences.en: Hello. This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好。这里是BBC英语教学的《6分钟英语》。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Georgie. If you're a 'Swiftie', that's a fan of pop star, Taylor Swift, her music rocks your world.
sentences.zh: 我是Phil。我是Georgie。如果你是一个“Swiftie”，也就是流行歌手Taylor Swift的粉丝，她的音乐会让你为之疯狂。

sentences.en: I like that phrase, ' rock your world', Phil.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那个短语，‘让你的世界为之摇滚’，Phil。

sentences.en: It means that something makes your life enjoyable, right?
sentences.zh: 它的意思是某事让你的生活变得愉快，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, yes but actually no, Georgie. I mean, Taylor Swift literally rocks the world!
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，但其实也不是，Georgie。我的意思是，Taylor Swift真的让世界摇滚了！

sentences.en: At a recent concert in Edinburgh, as part of Taylor Swift's 'Eras' tour, her fans' energetic dancing literally moved the Earth, with seismic activity usually associated with earthquakes detected four miles away!
sentences.zh: 在爱丁堡最近的一场演唱会上，作为Taylor Swift“时代”巡演的一部分，她粉丝们充满活力的舞蹈竟然让地球动了起来，检测到了通常与地震相关的地震活动，距离达四英里之远！

sentences.en: Yes, it's hard to believe, but in this programme we'll be hearing about the 'Swift-quake', a powerful force like an earthquake, coming not from nature, but from a pop concert!
sentences.zh: 是的，这很难让人相信，但在本期节目中，我们将听到关于“Swift-quake”的故事，这是一股类似于地震的强大力量，它不是来自大自然，而是来自流行音乐会！

sentences.en: And, as usual, we'll be learning some useful new vocabulary as well.
sentences.zh: 而且，和往常一样，我们也将学到一些有用的新词汇。

sentences.en: Great. But first I have a question for you, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 太好了。但首先我有一个问题要问你，Georgie。

sentences.en: Actually, Taylor Swift's Edinburgh show wasn't the first music concert to trigger seismic waves.
sentences.zh: 事实上，Taylor Swift的爱丁堡演出并不是第一场引发地震波的音乐会。

sentences.en: In 1992, the band Madness caused two earthquakes that saw local residents evacuated from their homes.
sentences.zh: 1992年，乐队Madness引发了两场地震，导致当地居民被迫撤离家园。

sentences.en: But at which London venue did the concert take place?
sentences.zh: 但是这场音乐会在哪个伦敦场地举行呢？

sentences.en: Was it: a) Hyde Park? b) The Royal Albert Hall? or c) Finsbury Park?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 海德公园？b) 皇家阿尔伯特音乐厅？还是 c) 芬斯伯里公园？

sentences.en: I'll guess the concert was held at the Royal Albert Hall.
sentences.zh: 我猜这场音乐会是在皇家阿尔伯特音乐厅举行的。

sentences.en: OK, Georgie, I'll reveal the correct answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，Georgie，我会在节目结束时揭晓正确答案。

sentences.en: Following Taylor Swift's Edinburgh concert, seismologists Emma Greenough and James Panton from Cardiff University, wanted to see if the same thing would happen at Taylor's concert in Cardiff.
sentences.zh: 在Taylor Swift的爱丁堡演唱会之后，来自卡迪夫大学的地震学家Emma Greenough和James Panton想要看看卡迪夫的Taylor演唱会上是否会发生同样的事情。

sentences.en: Seismologists are scientists who study earthquakes and seismic waves.
sentences.zh: 地震学家是研究地震和地震波的科学家。

sentences.en: Emma and James set up their equipment to monitor and record ground motion as the concert got started, as James explains here to Marnie Chesterton, presenter of BBC Radio 4 programme, 'Inside Science': Tell me about the peak on this graph that you're seeing, and what that actually corresponds to.
sentences.zh: Emma和James设置了他们的设备来监测和记录演唱会开始时的地面运动，正如James在这里向BBC Radio 4节目《走近科学》的主持人Marnie Chesterton所解释的那样：告诉我你在这个图表上看到的峰值，以及这究竟对应着什么。

sentences.en: In this top graph of the red wiggly line, we're looking at the ground velocity in essentially metres per second.
sentences.zh: 在这个红色波浪线的顶部图表中，我们本质上是在观察每秒米数的地面速度。

sentences.en: So, that's the velocity that the ground is vibrating up and down.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是地面上下振动的速度。

sentences.en: So, this is literally people stamping up and down.
sentences.zh: 所以，这字面意思是人们在上下跺脚。

sentences.en: Yes, so this is all of the energy combined from the 73,000 people in the stadium, jumping in unison and stamping in unison.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以这是体育场内73,000人齐声跳跃和齐声跺脚的所有能量的总和。

sentences.en: James, the British Geological Survey recorded 23.4 nanometres of movement in Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: James，英国地质调查局在爱丁堡记录了23.4纳米的移动。

sentences.en: What's that actually mean? So, what that means is that they recorded the ground flexing up and down by a distance of 23 nanometres.
sentences.zh: 这究竟是什么意思？所以，这意味着他们记录了地面上下弯曲了23纳米的距离。

sentences.en: James's equipment recorded seismic movement when Taylor Swift started to sing.
sentences.zh: 当Taylor Swift开始唱歌时，James的设备记录下了地震运动。

sentences.en: Her hit song, Cruel Summer, created a peak - the highest point - in the graph which James's machine was drawing.
sentences.zh: 她的热门歌曲《Cruel Summer》在James的机器正在绘制的图表中创造了一个峰值——最高点。

sentences.en: The peak was made by thousands of Swifties jumping up and down in unison, together and at the same time, creating something like a mini earthquake.
sentences.zh: 这个峰值是由成千上万的Swifties齐声、共同且同时上下跳跃产生的，创造了类似于微型地震的东西。

sentences.en: The seismologists measured a ground movement of 23 nanometres.
sentences.zh: 地震学家测量到地面移动了23纳米。

sentences.en: That may not sound much, but remember this is the earth itself actually flexing or bending without breaking.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能不算什么，但请记住，这是地球本身在没有破裂的情况下实际弯曲或屈曲。

sentences.en: So, the ground is shaking, music is blasting, and thousands of fans are dancing.
sentences.zh: 所以，地面在震动，音乐在轰鸣，成千上万的粉丝在跳舞。

sentences.en: But does this qualify as an earthquake, scientifically speaking?
sentences.zh: 但这在科学意义上算得上地震吗？

sentences.en: Here's James Panton and Marnie Chesterton again for BBC Radio 4's, Inside Science: James, impressive as this is to see coming up on your seismograph, this is not the same league really as an earthquake.
sentences.zh: 这里又是James Panton和Marnie Chesterton为BBC Radio 4的《走近科学》节目带来的内容：James，尽管看到这个出现在你的地震仪上让人印象深刻，但这跟地震真的不是一个等级的。

sentences.en: No, definitely not. There have been some people who have tried to convert the energy output from concerts into a local magnitude scale to make it comparable to an earthquake, and when that's happened, we find magnitudes that are generally less than one.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不是。曾有一些人试图将音乐会产生的能量输出转化为地方震级标度，使其与地震具有可比性，当这种情况发生时，我们发现震级通常小于一。

sentences.en: Sadly, the answer to Georgie's question is 'no' – the Taylor Swift concert wasn't technically an earthquake.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，Georgie的问题的答案是“否定”的——Taylor Swift的演唱会从技术上讲并不是一次地震。

sentences.en: Marnie says the concert was not in the same league, an idiom meaning not nearly as good or important as something else.
sentences.zh: Marnie说这场演唱会不在同一个等级，这是一个习语，意思是远不如其他东西那么好或重要。

sentences.en: Yes, the energy created by the music's sound waves and thousands of fans jumping did move the earth, but not in a way that's comparable, or similar, to a real earthquake.
sentences.zh: 是的，由音乐声波和成千上万粉丝跳跃产生的能量确实移动了地球，但其方式与真正的地震不具可比性，也不相似。

sentences.en: By definition, an earthquake must break the earth's crust, and is caused by either the movement of tectonic plates or a volcano.
sentences.zh: 根据定义，地震必须破裂地壳，并且是由板块运动或火山引起的。

sentences.en: Officially, Taylor Swift didn't cause an earthquake, but for the Swifties it probably felt like one!
sentences.zh: 官方上讲，Taylor Swift没有引发地震，但对于Swifties来说，感觉可能就像是一场地震！

sentences.en: All of which brings us back to my question, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都把我们带回了我的问题，Georgie。

sentences.en: I asked you about another earth-shattering concert involving the British band, Madness, but where in London did the show take place?
sentences.zh: 我问你关于另一场涉及英国乐队Madness的震撼人心的音乐会，但演出是在伦敦的什么地方举行 的？

sentences.en: And I guessed it was at The Royal Albert Hall.
sentences.zh: 我猜是在皇家阿尔伯特音乐厅。

sentences.en: Which was the wrong answer, I'm afraid, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 恐怕你猜错了，Georgie。

sentences.en: In fact, the concert happened in Finsbury Park.
sentences.zh: 事实上，演唱会发生在芬斯伯里公园。

sentences.en: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this programme starting with the phrase, rock your world, meaning that someone or something has a positive effect on you, making your life enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们回顾一下我们在本节目中学到的词汇，从短语“rock your world”（震撼你的世界）开始，意思是某人或某事对你产生积极的影响，让你的生活愉快。

sentences.en: A peak is the highest point of something.
sentences.zh: Peak（峰值）是某事物的最高点。

sentences.en: When things happen in unison, they happen together, at the same time.
sentences.zh: 当事情in unison（齐声/同步）发生时，它们是在同一时间一起发生的。

sentences.en: To flex means to bend without breaking. If you say something is not in the same league as something else, you mean it's nowhere near as good or important.
sentences.zh: Flex的意思是弯曲而不折断。如果你说某事is not in the same league as（与……不在同一个等级）其他事物，你的意思是它远不如后者那么好或重要。

sentences.en: And finally, the adjective comparable means similar in size, amount, or quality.
sentences.zh: 最后，形容词comparable（可比的）意为在大小、数量或质量上相似。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember to join us again next time for more trending topics and useful vocabulary, here at 6 Minute English.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了，但请记得下次再来加入我们，收听更多热门话题和有用的词汇，就在6分钟英语。

sentences.en: Goodbye for now! Bye!
sentences.zh: 先到这里，再见！再见！
